title: Weak factorization systems on finite direct diagrams
statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be a cocomplete category (one admitting every small colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) and let $(\mathcal L,\mathcal R)$ be a weak factorization system with functorial factorizations: every map factors functorially as a map in $\mathcal L$ followed by a map in $\mathcal R$, and each class is exactly the maps with the diagonal-lifting property against the other. Let $K$ have finitely many objects and morphisms and a natural-number degree strictly increased by nonidentity arrows. For $X:K\to\mathcal B$ set $L_kX=\operatorname{colim}_{(a:j\to k)\ne1_k}X_j$, with morphisms in the indexing category the commuting triangles over $k$. For $f:X\to Y$ let $\lambda_k(f):X_k\coprod_{L_kX}L_kY\to Y_k$. Then the maps for which all $\lambda_k(f)$ belong to $\mathcal L$, together with the maps that are objectwise in $\mathcal R$, form a weak factorization system with functorial factorizations on $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$. Every map in its left class is objectwise in $\mathcal L$, and its colimit map is in $\mathcal L$. This includes empty $K$ and also applies with any other finite direct category in place of $K$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Section 5.1, Proposition 5.1.4, Corollary 5.1.5 and proof of Theorem 5.1.3, printed pp. 121-122. The factorization and lifting induction uses only the specified weak factorization system, not both systems or weak equivalences. No Stacks tag states this diagram-WFS extension.
